items.title: The locus of the base where a closed map becomes unramified is an open subspace with the universal property
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram of algebraic spaces X -> Y -> Z with p : X -> Z locally of finite type and closed, the lemma produces an open subspace W of Z such that a morphism Z' -> Z factors through W exactly when the base changed map X_{Z'} -> Y_{Z'} is unramified. The retained proof is written: the where-unramified open U(f) of X exists with base-change-stable formation (Morphisms of Spaces, lemma where-unramified); define W as the open subspace (Properties of Spaces, lemma open-subspaces) whose points are Z minus the closed image p(|X| \ |U(f)|) — closedness of p is what makes the complement open; the universal property follows from the base-change stability of U(f) plus the factor-through-open-subspace criterion (Properties of Spaces, lemma factor-through-open-subspace). Retained author proof at lines 11543-11563.
